visualization.takeaway: For this refund, start with Postgres; the payment provider needs its own retry protection.
visualization.description: For the illustrated refund, start with Postgres: related customer balance, refund and approval records can commit in one transaction. Lakebase is a managed Postgres choice when Databricks integration matters. A support-case document groups messages, proposal and review state, but a separately stored balance needs an explicit cross-document design. MongoDB supports multi-document transactions; Cosmos DB document API batches share one logical partition key. A provider payment sits beyond either database transaction, requiring provider idempotency and a recoverable workflow. The duplicate-request control illustrates looking up a recorded operation rather than starting a new payment.

visualization.takeaway: Progress travels over SSE. Recovery depends on stored run state.
visualization.description: Read the lanes from agent to application to browser. The application checks access and records run state. Approval is a separate authenticated request. The disconnect example assumes that completion was recorded before the SSE connection dropped. Recovery reads the recorded run without blindly repeating the refund. These are illustrative application event names, not LangChain or AppKit API names. LangChain supplies agent events; AppKit also includes an app server and agent hosting, with the agents plugin in beta. Persistence and recovery must be implemented by the application.

title: A spoken promise is not a completed action

shareLine: A spoken promise is not a completed action.
ctaLabel: Discuss a workflow you would like to direct hands-free

proof.heading: Watch the Cargo demonstration
proof.description: In the documented Cargo workflow, a spoken request initiates recovery. The officer checks the sandbox service until it answers twice before reporting recovery. This depicts the recorded implementation, not a new run, participant study or general performance result.
proof.label: Inspect the implementation

media.caption: Previously recorded Cargo sandbox demonstration. The take uses prerecorded captain audio; it is not a participant accessibility study. On-screen dialogue appears in the recording.

transcript.intro: The captain interrupts the opening fleet briefing to select Cargo. The cockpit follows the conversation and highlights the service under discussion. Cargo moves from unavailable to recovery in progress, then answers the verification probes. The dialogue below starts at that interruption. Spoken figures belong to the saved briefing in this recording, not current analytics. The captain audio was prerecorded.

turns.speaker: First Officer
turns.text: Cargo stopped answering 1 minute ago. Bring it online, park it, or hear why?

turns.speaker: First Officer
turns.text: On it. Helm is bringing Cargo back online.

turns.speaker: First Officer
turns.text: Captain, Cargo answers again. Checked twice, 75 milliseconds. Five left. Next: agents outnumber people on NextRole. Shall we?

turns.speaker: First Officer
turns.text: In thirty days, agents called NextRole's tools 848 times. 71 people visited the site. Hand it to an agent, park it, or hear why?

turns.speaker: First Officer
turns.text: Calls peaked at 159 on 22 September, then fell to one on 28 September. Want more, or shall we decide?

turns.speaker: First Officer
turns.text: Handed over. On the live fleet an agent takes it from here. Four left. Next: intel is counting us as visitors. Shall we?

turns.speaker: First Officer
turns.text: Watch closed. Two decisions logged. Fair winds, Captain.
